value.zh: 太祖道武帝 太宗明元帝
value.en: Emperor Daowu the Grand Progenitor; Emperor Mingyuan the Grand Successor.
value.literal: Grand Progenitor Emperor Daowu; Grand Successor Emperor Mingyuan.

value.zh: 文帝諱沙漠汗，以國太子留洛陽。
value.en: Wen Emperor, taboo name Shamohan, stayed in Luoyang as hostage heir.
value.literal: Wen Emperor, taboo name Shamohan, remained in Luoyang as the state's heir.

value.zh: 後文帝以神元春秋已高，求歸。
value.en: Later, seeing Shenyuan's great age, Shamohan asked leave to go home.
value.literal: Later Wen Emperor, because Shenyuan's years were already advanced, requested to return.

value.zh: 晉武帝具禮護送。
value.en: Emperor Wu of Jin honored him with full ceremony and sent him homeward under escort.
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin treated him with full rites and escorted him on his way.

value.zh: 五十六年，文帝復如晉，其冬還國。
value.en: In the fifty-sixth year he visited Jin again and came back that winter.
value.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Wen Emperor again went to Jin; that winter he returned to his state.

value.zh: 晉征北將軍衛瓘以文帝雄異，恐為後患，請留不遣。
value.en: Jin's north-pacifying general Wei Guan, fearing Shamohan's formidable talent, asked that he be kept and not released.
value.literal: Wei Guan, General Who Subdues the North of Jin, because Wen Emperor was formidable and strange, feared he would be a later trouble and requested that he be detained and not sent back.

value.zh: 復請以金錦賂國之大人，令致間隙。
value.en: He also proposed bribing the tribal great men with gold and brocade to set them at odds with one another.
value.literal: He again requested that gold and brocade be used to bribe the great men of the state so as to sow divisions among them.

value.zh: 五十八年方遣帝。
value.en: Not until the fifty-eighth year was the heir allowed to depart.
value.literal: Only in the fifty-eighth year was the Emperor sent off.

value.zh: 神元使諸部大人詣陰館迎帝。
value.en: Shenyuan ordered the tribal chiefs to Yinyuan to welcome the heir home.
value.literal: Shenyuan had the great men of the tribes go to Yinyuan to welcome the Emperor.

value.zh: 酒酣，帝仰視飛鳥，飛丸落之。
value.en: Wine deep in the cup, the heir glanced up at a bird in flight and dropped it with a pellet.
value.literal: As the wine went deep, the Emperor looked up at a flying bird and brought it down with a pellet.

value.zh: 時國俗無彈，眾大驚，相謂曰：「太子被服同南夏，兼奇術絕人。
value.en: The people knew no slingshot; everyone was shaken and murmured, "The heir wears southern dress and commands arts no one here can match.
value.literal: At the time the nation's custom knew no slings; all were greatly alarmed and said to one another, "The heir dresses like the southern Xia and possesses wondrous arts beyond any man.

value.zh: 若繼國統，變易舊俗，吾等必不得志。」
value.en: If he inherits the realm and changes our customs, we will never prosper again."
value.literal: If he inherits the state and alters our old ways, we shall never have our will."

value.zh: 乃謀危害帝，並先馳還，曰：「太子引空弓而落飛鳥，似得晉人異法。」
value.en: They plotted against him and rode ahead with a story: "The heir shot an empty bow and felled a bird in flight, as if he had learned some Jin sorcery."
value.literal: Thereupon they plotted to harm the Emperor, and first galloped back, saying, "The heir drew an empty bow yet brought down a flying bird, as though he had obtained some strange method of the Jin people."

value.zh: 自帝在晉後，諸子愛寵，神元頗有所惑。
value.en: During Shamohan's long stay in Jin, his younger brothers won favor, and Shenyuan grew uncertain.
value.literal: After the Emperor had been in Jin, the other sons were favored and cherished, and Shenyuan was much perplexed.

value.zh: 及聞諸大人請，因曰：「當便除之。」
value.en: When the elders pressed their case, he said, "Then let him be killed at once."
value.literal: On hearing the great men's request, he therefore said, "He should be removed at once."

value.zh: 於是諸大人馳詣塞南，矯害帝。
value.en: The great men raced south of the frontier passes and murdered the heir under a forged order.
value.literal: Thereupon the great men galloped to the south of the passes and, by forged command, killed the Emperor.

value.zh: 其年，神元不豫。
value.en: That same year Shenyuan fell ill.
value.literal: In that year Shenyuan was unwell.

value.zh: 烏丸王庫賢親近任勢。
value.en: Kuxian, a Wuhuan king, stood close to the throne and held real power.
value.literal: Kuxian, king of the Wuhuan, was close at hand and wielded power.

value.zh: 先受衛瓘之貨，欲沮動諸部，因於庭中礪鉞斧，曰：「上恨汝曹讒殺太子，欲盡收諸大人長子殺之。」
value.en: Having taken Wei Guan's bribes, he meant to panic the tribes; in the courtyard he sharpened axe and blade, crying, "The High One blames you for the heir's murder and will seize every chief's eldest son and kill him."
value.literal: He had earlier accepted bribes from Wei Guan and wished to stir up the various tribes; therefore in the courtyard he sharpened axe and hatchet, saying, "The High One resents you all for slandering and killing the heir; he intends to seize every great man's eldest sons and put them to death."

value.zh: 大人皆信，各各散走。
value.en: The chiefs believed him and fled in every direction.
value.literal: The great men all believed it; each scattered and fled.

value.zh: 神元尋崩，凡饗國五十八年，年一百四歲。
value.en: Shenyuan died soon after, having ruled fifty-eight years and lived to one hundred and four.
value.literal: Shenyuan soon died; in all he had ruled the state fifty-eight years, and his years reached one hundred and four.

value.zh: 道武即位，尊為始祖。
value.en: When Daowu came to power he enshrined Shenyuan as the dynastic Progenitor.
value.literal: When Daowu took the throne he honored him as Progenitor.

value.zh: 子章皇帝悉鹿立，時諸部離叛。
value.en: His son Zhang Emperor Silu succeeded while the tribes were splintering away.
value.literal: His son Zhang Emperor Silu succeeded; at the time the tribes were breaking away.

value.zh: 帝九年而崩。
value.en: Silu reigned nine years and died.
value.literal: The Emperor died in the ninth year.

value.zh: 弟平皇帝綽立，七年而崩。
value.en: His brother Ping Emperor Chuo ruled seven years and died.
value.literal: His younger brother Ping Emperor Chuo succeeded; in seven years he died.

value.zh: 文帝少子思皇帝立，思皇帝諱弗。
value.en: Wen Emperor's youngest son, Si Emperor, came next; Si Emperor's taboo name was Fu.
value.literal: The youngest son of Wen Emperor, Si Emperor, succeeded; Si Emperor, taboo name Fu.

value.zh: 政崇寬簡，百姓懷服。
value.en: He governed with leniency and ease, and the people gave him their hearts.
value.literal: His government honored leniency and simplicity; the common people were attached and submitted.

value.zh: 一年而崩。
value.en: He died after a single year.
value.literal: In one year he died.

value.zh: 神元子昭帝祿官立。
value.en: Shenyuan's son Zhao Emperor Luguan took the throne.
value.literal: Shenyuan's son Zhao Emperor Luguan succeeded.

value.zh: 帝元年，分國為三部：一居上穀北，濡源西，東接宇文部，自統之；
value.en: In his first year Luguan split the realm in three: one branch lived north of Shanggu and west of Ruyuan, adjoining the Yuwen, under his own hand;
value.literal: In the first year of the Emperor he divided the state into three parts: one group dwelt north of Shanggu, west of Ruyuan, bordering the Yuwen tribe, and he ruled them himself;

value.zh: 一居代郡之參合陂北，使文帝長子桓帝諱猗厓統之；
value.en: one camped north of Canhe Marsh in Dai commandery, ruled by Wen Emperor's eldest son Huan Emperor, taboo name Yiyu;
value.literal: one dwelt north of Canhebo in Dai commandery, and he had Wen Emperor's eldest son Huan Emperor, taboo name Yiyu, rule them;

value.zh: 一居定襄之盛樂故城，使桓帝弟穆帝猗盧統之。
value.en: one occupied old Shengle in Dingxiang, ruled by Huan Emperor's younger brother Mu Emperor Yilu.
value.literal: one dwelt at the old city of Shengle in Dingxiang, and he had Huan Emperor's younger brother Mu Emperor Yilu rule them.

value.zh: 景皇帝諱師，字子元，宣帝長子也。
value.en: Emperor Jing, whose personal name was Shi and courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan of Jin.
value.literal: Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan.

value.zh: 雅有風彩，沈毅多大略。
value.en: He carried himself with quiet distinction, steady and resolute, with a strategist’s breadth of mind.
value.literal: He had refined bearing and presence, was deep and resolute, and possessed great strategic vision.

value.zh: 少流美譽，與夏侯玄、何晏齊名。
value.en: While still young he was widely praised, and his name stood alongside those of Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.
value.literal: In youth he enjoyed a fine reputation, and was ranked with Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.

value.zh: 晏常稱曰：「惟幾也能成天下之務，司馬子元是也。」
value.en: He Yan used to say, "It takes someone who senses the moment before it turns to carry the weight of the realm—and that man is Sima Ziyuan."
value.literal: He Yan often declared, "Only one who apprehends subtle turning points can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; Sima Ziyuan is such a man."

value.zh: 魏景初中，拜散騎常侍，累遷中護軍。
value.en: During Wei’s Jingchu years he received appointment as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and rose step by step to Central Protector of the Army.
value.literal: In the Jingchu era of Wei, he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and eventually promoted to Central Protector of the Army.

value.zh: 為選用之法，舉不越功，吏無私焉。
value.en: He set rules for appointments so that promotions matched real achievement, and his staff could not trade on personal connections.
value.literal: He established methods for selection and appointment; recommendations did not exceed actual merit, and clerks practiced no private favoritism.

value.zh: 宣穆皇后崩，居喪以至孝聞。
value.en: After Empress Dowager Xuanmu’s death, he kept mourning with such scrupulous grief that word of his filial piety spread everywhere.
value.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanmu died, he observed mourning for her and was famed for extreme filial devotion.

value.zh: 宣帝之將誅曹爽，深謀秘策，獨與帝潛畫，文帝弗之知也。
value.en: As Sima Yi readied the strike against Cao Shuang, he laid his plans in the deepest secrecy—working them out alone with Sima Shi—while Sima Zhao was kept entirely in the dark.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to execute Cao Shuang, with deep plots and secret stratagems he secretly planned only with the Emperor (Sima Shi); Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao) did not know of it.

value.zh: 將發夕乃告之，既而使人覘之，帝寢如常，而文帝不能安席。
value.en: Sima Yi waited until the night before the coup to inform his son; when he sent men to watch Sima Shi’s quarters, Shi slept soundly as on any other night, while Sima Zhao tossed and could not settle.
value.literal: On the eve of launching the action he was told; then someone was sent to spy on him—the Emperor slept as usual, but Emperor Wen could not find rest on his mat.

value.zh: 晨會兵司馬門，鎮靜內外，置陣甚整。
value.en: At daybreak he drew up his forces at the Sima Gate, steadying the palace inside and out and arraying them with flawless discipline.
value.literal: At dawn he assembled troops at the Sima Gate, calming inside and outside, and deployed formations in very good order.

value.zh: 宣帝曰：「此子竟可也。」
value.en: Sima Yi said, "This boy will do after all."
value.literal: Emperor Xuan said, "This son is indeed capable."

value.zh: 初，帝陰養死士三千，散在人間，至是一朝而集，眾莫知所出也。
value.en: Earlier, Sima Shi had quietly kept three thousand devoted fighters dispersed through the capital; now they materialized overnight, and no one could guess where they had sprung from.
value.literal: At the outset the Emperor had secretly maintained three thousand bravos, scattered among the people; at this moment they gathered in a single morning, and the multitude did not know whence they had come.

value.zh: 事平，以功封長平鄉侯，食邑千戶，尋加衛將軍。
value.en: After the coup succeeded he was rewarded with the village marquisate of Changping and a thousand-household fief, and before long was named General of the Guard as well.
value.literal: When the affair was settled, by merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changping with a fief of one thousand households; soon he was additionally appointed General of the Guard.

value.zh: 及宣帝薨，議者咸云「伊尹既卒，伊陟嗣事」，天子命帝以撫軍大將軍輔政。
value.en: At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor appointed Sima Shi General Who Pacifies the Army to assist in government.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, those who deliberated all said, "After Yi Yin died, Yi Zhi succeeded to his duties," and the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor as General Who Stabilizes the Army and Great General to assist in government.

value.zh: 魏嘉平四年春正月，遷大將軍，加侍中，持節、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。
value.en: In the first month of spring, Wei’s fourth year of Jiaping, he advanced to Great General, was given the concurrent post of Palace Attendant, received the imperial baton, took overall command of central and frontier forces, and assumed control of the Secretariat.
value.literal: In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Jiaping of Wei, he was promoted to Great General, added as Palace Attendant, bearing credentials, supervising all military affairs of the central command and the regions, and recording Director of the Secretariat business.

value.zh: 命百官舉賢才，明少長，恤窮獨，理廢滯。
value.en: He instructed every office to put forward able men, to sort seniority fairly, to relieve the widowed and alone, and to clear the backlog of neglected business.
value.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to recommend worthy talent, clarify precedence of young and old, show pity to the destitute and solitary, and straighten out stalled appointments.

value.zh: 諸葛誕、毌丘儉、王昶、陳泰、胡遵都督四方，王基、州泰、鄧艾、石苞典州郡，盧毓、李豐裳選舉，傅嘏、虞松參計謀，鐘會、夏侯玄、王肅、陳本、孟康、趙酆、張緝預朝議，四海傾注，朝野肅然。
value.en: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun held regional commands; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao ran the provinces; Lu Yu and Li Feng handled personnel; Fu Gu and Yu Song shaped policy; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji sat in on the great councils. The empire fixed its hopes on them, and court and countryside grew solemn.
value.literal: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun supervised the four quarters; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao administered prefectures and commanderies; Lu Yu and Li Feng oversaw selection and appointment; Fu Gu and Yu Song joined in planning stratagems; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji took part in court deliberations; the four seas turned their gaze upon them, and court and countryside stood in solemn awe.

value.zh: 或有請改易制度者，帝曰：「'不識不知，順帝之則'，詩人之美也。
value.en: When voices rose for sweeping institutional change, Sima Shi answered, "The Odes praise the ruler who does not meddle for show but simply follows the pattern Heaven set for the sage-kings.
value.literal: When some requested changes to institutions, the Emperor said: "'Not knowing, not perceiving, following the norms of the Di'—that is what the poets praise.

value.zh: 三祖典制，所宜遵奉；
value.en: The precedents left by the three Wei founders are what we are bound to honor;
value.literal: The regulations of the three founding ancestors are what ought to be obeyed and upheld;

value.zh: 自非軍事，不得妄有改革。」
value.en: and apart from what war demands, nothing should be changed on a whim."
value.literal: unless it be military affairs, one must not recklessly carry out reforms."

value.zh: 咸熙元年春正月，檻車征艾。
value.en: In the first month of spring, Xianxi year 1, Deng Ai was summoned back in a prison cart.
value.literal: First year of Xianxi, spring, first month, caged cart summoned Ai.

value.zh: 乙丑，帝奉天子西征，次於長安。
value.en: On yichou he escorted the emperor west and encamped at Chang’an.
value.literal: On yichou, the Emperor escorting the Son of Heaven west campaigned, halted at Chang'an.

value.zh: 是時魏諸王侯悉在鄴城，命從事中郎山濤行軍司事，鎮於鄴，遣護軍賈充持節、督諸軍，據漢中。
value.en: With every Wei prince gathered at Yecheng, he put Shan Tao in charge of rear-area command there and sent Jia Chong with baton to oversee the armies holding Hanzhong.
value.literal: At this time Wei various princes and marquises were all at Yecheng; he ordered Retainer Shan Tao to conduct army affairs, garrisoning at Yecheng; sent Army Protector Jia Chong bearing credentials, supervising the various armies, occupying Hanzhong.

value.zh: 鐘會遂反於蜀，監軍衛瓘、右將軍胡烈攻會，斬之。
value.en: Zhong Hui rose in Shu; Wei Guan and Hu Lie struck him down and took his head.
value.literal: Zhong Hui then rebelled in Shu; Army Supervisor Wei Guan, General of the Right Hu Lie attacked Hui, beheaded him.

value.zh: 初，會之伐蜀也，西曹屬邵悌言於帝曰：「鐘會難信，不可令行。」
value.en: At first, when Zhong Hui was attacking Shu, Shao Ti, subordinate of the Western Bureau, said to Sima Zhao, "Zhong Hui is hard to trust; he must not be allowed to go."
value.literal: At first, when Zhong Hui was attacking Shu, Shao Ti, subordinate of the Western Bureau, said to Sima Zhao, "Zhong Hui is hard to trust; he must not be allowed to go."

value.zh: 帝笑曰：「取蜀如指掌，而眾人皆言不可，唯會與吾意同。
value.en: Sima Zhao had only smiled and said, "Shu will fall as easily as reading one’s palm, though everyone else doubted—only Zhong Hui shared my view.
value.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "Taking Shu is like pointing at the palm; yet the host of men all say it cannot be done; only Hui and Our intent agree.

value.zh: 滅蜀之後，中國將士，人自思歸，蜀之遺黎，猶懷震恐，縱有異志，無能為也。」
value.en: After Shu fell, every northern soldier would pine for home and the Shu populace would still quake with fear—even if someone harbored treason, he could do nothing with it."
value.literal: After extinguishing Shu, central state's officers and soldiers, each person thinks of returning; Shu's surviving common people still cherish trembling fear; even if they had different intent, they have no ability to act.

value.zh: 卒如所量。
value.en: Events proved him exactly right.
value.literal: In the end it was as he had measured.

value.zh: 丙辰，帝至自長安。
value.en: On bingchen he returned from Chang’an to the capital.
value.literal: On bingchen, the Emperor arrived from Chang'an.

value.zh: 三月己卯，進帝爵為王，增封並前二十郡。
value.en: On jimao in the third month he was raised from duke to king with twenty commanderies in all, old grants and new.
value.literal: Third month, day jimao, advanced the Emperor's noble rank to king, increased fief together with the previous twenty commanderies.

value.zh: 夏五月癸未，天子追加舞陽宣文侯為晉宣王，舞陽忠武侯為晉景王。
value.en: On guiwei in the fifth month of summer the emperor posthumously raised Sima Yi to Prince Xuan of Jin and Sima Shi to Prince Jing of Jin.
value.literal: Summer, fifth month, day guiwei, the Son of Heaven posthumously added Wuyang Marquis Xuanwen as Jin King Xuan, Wuyang Marquis Zhongwu as Jin King Jing.

value.zh: 秋七月，帝奏司空荀顗定禮儀，中護軍賈充正法律，尚書僕射裴秀議官制，太保鄭沖總而裁焉。
value.en: In the seventh month of autumn he charged Xun Yi with the rites, Jia Chong with the laws, Pei Xiu with the bureaucracy, and Zheng Chong as coordinator over all.
value.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Emperor memorialized Minister of Works Xun Yi to fix rites and ceremonies, Central Army Protector Jia Chong to rectify laws and statutes, Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu to deliberate official system, Grand Guardian Zheng Chong overall to judge them.

value.zh: 始建五等爵。
value.en: He began the institution of the five orders of nobility.
value.literal: For the first time established the five ranks of nobility.

value.zh: 冬十月丁亥，奏遣吳人相國參軍徐劭、散騎常侍水曹屬孫彧使吳，喻孫皓以平蜀之事，致馬錦等物，以示威懷。
value.en: On dinghai in the tenth winter month he memorialized to send Xu Shao and Sun Yu—Wu natives in his service—to Wu with horses and brocade, to tell Sun Hao of Shu’s fall and to blend threat with kindness.
value.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dinghai, memorialized to send Wu man Chancellor of State Army Advisor Xu Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Water Bureau Subordinate Sun Yu as envoys to Wu, informing Sun Hao of the affair of pacifying Shu, presenting horses, brocade, and such objects, in order to show awe and cherishing.

value.zh: 丙午，天子命中撫軍新昌鄉侯炎為晉世子。
value.en: On bingwu the emperor named Sima Yan, the Central Stabilizing General and Marquis of Xinchang township, heir apparent of Jin.
value.literal: On bingwu, the Son of Heaven ordered Central General Who Stabilizes the Army, village marquis of Xinchang Yan, to be Jin heir apparent.

value.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。
value.en: The emperor honored posthumously as Wu bore the personal name Yan and the courtesy name Anshi; he was the firstborn son of Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao).
value.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

value.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。
value.en: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.
value.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.

value.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。
value.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
value.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.

value.zh: 迎常道鄉公於東武陽，遷中撫軍，進封新昌鄉侯。
value.en: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinchang.
value.literal: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinchang.

value.zh: 及晉國建，立爲世子，拜撫軍大將軍，開府、副貳相國。
value.en: When the Jin state was founded, he was established as heir apparent, appointed Great General Who Pacifies the Army with an office of his own, and made second-in-command assisting the Minister of State.
value.literal: When the state of Jin was founded he was established as heir apparent, appointed great general who pacifies the army with independent command, and served as deputy to the minister of state.

value.zh: 丁卯，遣太僕劉原告于太廟。
value.en: On dingmao he dispatched grand coachman Liu Yuan to report to the imperial temple.
value.literal: On dingmao he sent grand coachman Liu Yuan to announce the matter in the grand temple.

value.zh: 封魏帝爲陳留王，邑萬戶，居於鄴宮；
value.en: The last Wei sovereign became king of Chenliu with a fief of ten thousand households, residing at Ye.
value.literal: He enfeoffed the Wei emperor as king of Chenliu, with ten thousand households, dwelling in the Ye palace;

value.zh: 魏氏諸王皆爲縣侯。
value.en: Every other Wei prince was reduced to county marquis.
value.literal: All kings of the house of Wei were made county marquises.

value.zh: 追尊宣王爲宣皇帝，景王爲景皇帝，文王爲文皇帝，宣王妃張氏爲宣穆皇后。
value.en: He posthumously honored King Xuan as Emperor Xuan, King Jing as Emperor Jing, and King Wen as Emperor Wen, and honored Lady Zhang, consort of King Xuan, as Empress Xuanmu.
value.literal: He posthumously honored king Xuan as emperor Xuan, king Jing as emperor Jing, king Wen as emperor Wen, and king Xuan’s consort, lady Zhang, as empress Xuanmu.

value.zh: 尊太妃王氏曰皇太后，宮曰崇化。
value.en: Lady Wang, the grand consort, became empress dowager with her palace named Chonghua.
value.literal: He honored grand consort Wang as empress dowager, her residence titled Chonghua.

value.zh: 封皇叔祖父孚爲安平王，皇叔父幹爲平原王，亮爲扶風王，伷爲東莞王，駿爲汝陰王，肜爲梁王，倫爲琅邪王，皇弟攸爲齊王，鑒爲樂安王，機爲燕王，[1]皇從伯父望爲義陽王，皇從叔父輔爲渤海王，晃爲下邳王，瑰爲太原王，珪爲高陽王，衡爲常山王，子文爲沛王，[2]泰爲隴西王，權爲彭城王，綏爲范陽王，遂爲濟南王，遜爲譙王，睦爲中山王，陵爲北海王，斌爲陳王，皇從父兄洪爲河間王，皇從父弟楙爲東平王。
value.en: He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping; his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ruyin, Tong as king of Liang, and Lun as king of Langye; his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Lean, and Ji as king of Yan; [1] his father's elder cousin Wang as king of Yiyang; his father's younger cousins Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, and Bin as king of Chen; his elder cousin Hong as king of Hejian; and his younger cousin Mao as king of Dongping.
value.literal: He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping, his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ru'yin, Tong as king of Liang, Lun as king of Langye, his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Le'an, Ji as king of Yan, [1] his cousin once removed Wang as king of Yiyang, his father's younger cousins Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, and Bin as king of Chen, his cousin Hong as king of Hejian, and his cousin Mao as king of Dongping.

value.zh: 以驃騎將軍石苞爲大司馬，封樂陵公，車騎將軍陳騫爲高平公，衛將軍賈充爲車騎將軍、魯公，尚書令裴秀爲鉅鹿公，侍中荀勖爲濟北公，太保鄭沖爲太傅、壽光公，太尉王祥爲太保、睢陵公，丞相何曾爲太尉、朗陵公，御史大夫王沈爲驃騎將軍、博陵公，司空荀顗爲臨淮公，鎮北大將軍衛瓘爲菑陽公。
value.en: He appointed Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry, grand marshal and duke of Leling; Chen Qian duke of Gaoping; Jia Chong general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Lu; Pei Xiu duke of Julu; Xun Xu duke of Jibei; Zheng Chong grand tutor and duke of Shouguang; Wang Xiang grand guardian and duke of Suiling; He Zeng grand commandant and duke of Langling; Wang Chen general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling; Xun Yi duke of Linhuai; and Wei Guan duke of Ziyang.
value.literal: He appointed Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry, as grand marshal with enfeoffment as duke of Leling; Chen Qian, general of chariots and cavalry, as duke of Gaoping; Jia Chong, guard general, as general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Lu; Pei Xiu, supervisor of the masters of writing, as duke of Julu; Xun Xu, palace attendant, as duke of Jibei; Zheng Chong, grand guardian, as grand tutor and duke of Shouguang; Wang Xiang, grand commandant, as grand protector and duke of Suiling; He Zeng, chancellor, as grand commandant and duke of Langling; Wang Chen, imperial counselor, as general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling; Xun Yi, minister of works, as duke of Linhuai; Wei Guan, great general who guards the north, as duke of Ziyang.

value.zh: 其餘增封進爵各有差，文武普增位二等。
value.en: Others were promoted in title by degrees, and the whole bureaucracy gained two steps in rank.
value.literal: The rest received increased fiefs and advanced noble ranks each according to difference; civil and military officials were universally advanced two grades in rank.

value.zh: 改景初曆爲太始曆，臘以酉，社以丑。
value.en: The calendar was renamed from Jingchu to Taishi; the year-end rite was fixed in you and the soil altar in chou.
value.literal: He changed the Jingchu calendar to the Taishi calendar, with year-end sacrifice in the you hour and earth god in the chou hour.

value.zh: 二月，以雍州隴右五郡及涼州之金城、梁州之陰平置秦州。
value.en: In the second month he carved out Qin province, combining the five Longyou commanderies under Yong with Jincheng from the Hexi frontier and Yinping from the Hanzhong basin.
value.literal: In the second month Qin province was established from the five commanderies of Yongzhou west of the Long Range, together with Jincheng commandery from the northwest frontier and Yinping commandery from the Hanzhong uplands.

value.zh: 辛巳，白龍二見於趙國。
value.en: On xinsi two white dragons appeared in Zhao.
value.literal: On the day xinsi two white dragons were seen in the principality of Zhao.

value.zh: 青、徐、兗三州水，遣使振恤之。
value.en: Flooding struck Qing, Xu, and Yan; the court dispatched inspectors with grain and aid.
value.literal: The provinces of Qing, Xu, and Yan suffered floods; envoys were sent to relieve them.

value.zh: 壬寅，以尚書左僕射羊祜都督荊州諸軍事，征東大將軍衛瓘都督青州諸軍事，東莞王伷鎮東大將軍、都督徐州諸軍事。
value.en: On renyin Yang Hu took command on the Jing front, Wei Guan on the Qing front, and Sima Zhou of Dongguan became commander-in-chief on the Xu front.
value.literal: On the day renyin, Yang Hu, senior vice-director of the masters of the left, was appointed to supervise all military affairs of Jing province; Wei Guan, great general who campaigns east, was appointed to supervise all military affairs of Qing province; king Zhou of Dongguan was made great general who guards the east and supervisor of all military affairs of Xu province.

value.zh: 丁亥，詔曰：「古者歲書群吏之能否，三年而誅賞之。
value.en: On dinghai, an edict said, "In antiquity, each year the ability or inability of the assembled clerks was written down, and after three years they were punished or rewarded.
value.literal: On the day dinghai an edict said: “In antiquity the year’s record set down whether host of clerks could or could not perform their duties; after three years they were executed or rewarded.

value.zh: 諸令史前後，但簡遣疏劣，而無有勸進，非黜陟之謂也。
value.en: So far prefects had only purged the useless without promoting the able—that was not true evaluation.
value.literal: Among the clerks of the various prefectures, hitherto only the slack and inferior were winnowed out and dismissed, while there was no encouragement of advancement—this is not what demotion and promotion mean.

value.zh: 其條勤能有稱尤異者，歲以爲常。
value.en: Any clerk praised year after year for diligence and talent should be entered on a standing honor roll.
value.literal: Let those whose diligence and ability win praise as outstanding be recorded annually as a constant rule.

value.zh: 吾將議其功勞。」
value.en: The throne will then weigh rewards for proven service.”
value.literal: I shall deliberate their merit and labor.”

value.zh: 己未，詔蜀相諸葛亮孫京隨才署吏。
value.en: On jiwei, Zhuge Liang's grandson Zhuge Jing was assigned an office suited to his talents.
value.literal: On jiwei, an edict ordered that Zhuge Jing, grandson of Zhuge Liang, chancellor of Shu, be appointed to office according to his abilities.

value.zh: 三月，平虜護軍文淑討叛虜樹機能等，並破之。
value.en: Third month: Wen Shu, Protector-general Who Pacifies the Captives, defeated the rebel forces of Shujineng and the others.
value.literal: In the third month, Wen Shu, Protector-general Who Pacifies the Captives, campaigned against the rebel captives Shujineng and the others and defeated them all.

value.zh: 有星孛于胃。
value.en: A comet trailed through the Wei mansion.
value.literal: A broom star appeared in the asterism Wei.

value.zh: 乙未，帝將射雉，慮損麥苗而止。
value.en: Yiwei: he canceled a hunt lest arrows trample the wheat.
value.literal: On the day yiwei the emperor was about to shoot pheasants but stopped, fearing damage to the wheat.

value.zh: 冬十月，以征北大將軍衛瓘爲尚書令。
value.en: Winter: northern commander Wei Guan took over the secretariat.
value.literal: In winter, the tenth month Wei Guan, great general who campaigns north, was appointed supervisor of the masters of writing.

value.zh: 揚州刺史應綽伐吳皖城，斬首五千級，焚穀米百八十萬斛。
value.en: Ying Chuo stormed Wu’s Wan stronghold, counted five thousand kills, and torched nearly two million hu of enemy stores.
value.literal: Ying Chuo, inspector of Yang province, attacked Wu’s fortress at Wan, took five thousand heads, and burned one million eight hundred thousand hu of grain and rice.

value.zh: 冬十二月甲申，以司空齊王攸爲大司馬、督青州諸軍事，鎮東大將軍、琅邪王伷爲撫軍大將軍，[32]汝南王亮爲太尉，光祿大夫山濤爲司徒，尚書令衛瓘爲司空。
value.en: Winter, twelfth month, jiashen: Sima You, King of Qi and Minister of Works, was made Grand Marshal and supervisor of all military affairs in Qing province; Sima Zhou, Great General Who Garrisons the East and King of Langye, was made Great General Who Pacifies the Army; [32] Sima Liang, King of Runan, was made Grand Commandant; Shan Tao, Grand Master of Brilliant Prosperity, was made Minister over the Masses; and Wei Guan, Director of the Secretariat, was made Minister of Works.
value.literal: On the day jiashen of winter, twelfth month, Sima You, king of Qi and minister of works, was made grand marshal and supervisor of all military affairs of Qing province; Sima Zhou, great general who guards the east and king of Langye, was made great general who pacifies the army [32]; Sima Liang, king of Runan, grand commandant; Shan Tao, grand officer of brilliant prosperity, steward of the masters of the people; Wei Guan, supervisor of the masters of writing, minister of works.

value.zh: 丙申，詔四方水旱甚者無出田租。
value.en: Bingshen: disaster counties were forgiven their grain rent.
value.literal: On the day bingshen an edict ordered that regions suffering severe flood or drought pay no field rent.

value.zh: 是歲，東夷絕遠三十餘國、西南夷二十餘國來獻。
value.en: Embassies arrived from thirty-plus eastern and twenty-plus southwestern tribes.
value.literal: That year more than thirty distant eastern Yi states and more than twenty southwestern Yi states came to present tribute.

value.zh: 虜奚軻男女十萬口來降。
value.en: A hundred thousand Xike tribespeople submitted to Jin.
value.literal: One hundred thousand persons, men and women, of the Xike tribe came to surrender.

value.en: Manuscripts mark editorial note [40] here.
value.literal: [40] The received text carries commentary marker [40] at this point.

value.zh: 八月丙戌，以征東大將軍衛瓘爲征北大將軍、都督幽州諸軍事。
value.en: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Wei Guan was moved from General-in-chief Who Campaigns East to General-in-chief Who Campaigns North and given command of Youzhou military affairs.
value.literal: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Wei Guan, General-in-chief Who Campaigns East, was made General-in-chief Who Campaigns North and Area Commander of military affairs in Youzhou.

value.zh: 丙申，城陽王憲薨。
value.en: On bingshen, Prince Xian of Chengyang died.
value.literal: On bingshen, Xian, Prince of Chengyang, died.

value.zh: 分益州之南中四郡置寧州，曲赦四郡殊死已下。
value.en: The four Nanzhong commanderies were detached from Yizhou to form Ningzhou, and a special amnesty there covered capital offenders and below.
value.literal: The four Nanzhong commanderies of Yizhou were separated to establish Ningzhou, and within the four commanderies those sentenced to death and below were specially pardoned.

value.zh: 三年春正月丙子朔，日有蝕之。
value.en: In the third year, spring, first month, on the bingzi new moon, the sun was eclipsed.
value.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, on the bingzi new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.

value.zh: 立皇子裕爲始平王，安平穆王隆弟敦爲安平王。
value.en: The emperor made his son Yu prince of Shiping and made Dun, younger brother of Long, Prince Mu of Anping, prince of Anping.
value.literal: The imperial son Yu was established as Prince of Shiping, and Dun, younger brother of Long, Prince Mu of Anping, was established as Prince of Anping.

value.zh: 詔曰：「宗室戚屬，國之枝葉，欲令奉率德義，爲天下式。
value.en: An edict declared: "The imperial kin are the state's branches and leaves; they should uphold virtue and righteousness and serve as models for the realm.
value.literal: An edict said: "The imperial clan and kin by marriage are the branches and leaves of the state; I wish to have them uphold and lead in virtue and righteousness, becoming a model for the realm.

value.zh: 然處富貴而能慎行者寡，召穆公糾合兄弟而賦唐棣之詩，此姬氏所以本枝百世也。
value.en: Yet few men in wealth and rank remain careful. Lord Mu of Shao gathered his brothers and sang Tangdi; by such means the Ji clan preserved root and branch for generations.
value.literal: Yet few who occupy wealth and rank can conduct themselves cautiously; Lord Mu of Shao gathered his brothers and composed the poem Tangdi, and this was how the Ji lineage kept root and branch for a hundred generations.

value.zh: 今以衛將軍、扶風王亮爲宗師，所當施行，皆諮之於宗師也。」
value.en: I now appoint Liang, Prince of Fufeng and Guards General, as Master of the Clan; all clan measures are to be referred to him."
value.literal: Now I make the Guards General, Liang, Prince of Fufeng, Master of the Clan; all measures to be carried out shall be consulted with the Master of the Clan."

value.zh: 庚寅，始平王裕薨。
value.en: On gengyin, Prince Yu of Shiping died.
value.literal: On gengyin, Yu, Prince of Shiping, died.

value.zh: 有星孛於西方。
value.en: A comet appeared in the west.
value.literal: There was a broom star in the west.

value.zh: 使征北大將軍衛瓘討鮮卑力微。
value.en: Wei Guan, General-in-chief Who Campaigns North, was sent against the Xianbei leader Liwei.
value.literal: He sent Wei Guan, General-in-chief Who Campaigns North, to campaign against Liwei of the Xianbei.

value.zh: 太熙元年春正月辛酉朔，改元。
value.en: In Taixi 1, spring, first month, on the xinyou new moon, the reign title was changed.
value.literal: In Taixi 1, spring, first month, on the xinyou new moon, the reign period was changed.

value.zh: 己巳，以尚書左僕射王渾爲司徒，司空衛瓘爲太保。
value.en: On jisi, Wang Hun was promoted from Left Supervisor of the Secretariat to Minister over the Masses, and Wei Guan from Minister of Works to Grand Protector.
value.literal: On jisi, Wang Hun, Left Supervisor of the Secretariat, was made Minister over the Masses, and Wei Guan, Minister of Works, was made Grand Protector.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 三月辛卯，誅太傅楊駿，駿弟衛將軍珧，太子太保濟，中護軍張劭，散騎常侍段廣、楊邈，左將軍劉預，河南尹李斌，中書令蔣俊，東夷校尉文淑，尚書武茂，皆夷三族。
value.en: In the third month Yang Jun and his entire faction were put to death: his brother Yang Yao, Yang Ji, Zhang Shao, Duan Guang, Yang Miao, Liu Yu, Li Bin, Jiang Jun, Wen Shu, and Wu Mao, with every branch of their families extirpated.
value.literal: In the third month, on the xinmao day, Grand Tutor Yang Jun was executed; Jun’s younger brother General of the Guards Yang Yao, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent Yang Ji, Central Protector of the Army Zhang Shao, Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary Duan Guang and Yang Miao, General of the Left Liu Yu, Intendant of Henan Li Bin, Director of the Secretariat Jiang Jun, Colonel of Eastern Yi Tribes Wen Shu, and Minister Wu Mao—all were exterminated to the third degree of kin.

value.zh: 壬辰，大赦，改元。
value.en: A general amnesty followed, and the reign title was changed again.
value.literal: On the renchen day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

value.zh: 賈后矯詔廢皇太后爲庶人，徙于金墉城，告于天地宗廟。
value.en: Empress Jia forged an edict that stripped the empress dowager of her title, confined her in the Jinyong fortress, and had the act proclaimed to Heaven, Earth, and the imperial shrines.
value.literal: Empress Jia forged an edict deposing the empress dowager to commoner status, transferring her to the Jinyong Fortress, and reported it to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

value.zh: 誅太后母龐氏。
value.en: The dowager’s mother, Lady Pang, was executed.
value.literal: The empress dowager’s mother, the Lady Pang, was executed.

value.zh: 壬寅，徵大司馬、汝南王亮爲太宰，與太保衛瓘輔政。
value.en: Prince Liang of Runan was recalled from the grand marshal’s post to serve as grand steward alongside Grand Guardian Wei Guan as coregent.
value.literal: On the renyin day, Grand Marshal, Prince Liang of Runan, was summoned to be grand steward, and together with Grand Guardian Wei Guan assisted the government.

value.zh: 以秦王柬爲大將軍，東平王楙爲撫軍大將軍，鎮南將軍、楚王瑋爲衛將軍，領北軍中候，下邳王晃爲尚書令，東安公繇爲尚書左僕射，進封東安王。
value.en: Prince Jian of Qin took the supreme military command; Prince Mao of Dongping became general who soothes the army; Prince Wei of Chu became general of the guards and colonel of the northern camp; Prince Huang of Xiapi headed the secretariat; Duke Yao of Dong’an became its senior deputy and was raised to prince of Dong’an.
value.literal: Prince Jian of Qin was made general-in-chief; Prince Mao of Dongping was made general-in-chief who soothes the army; General Who Guards the South, Prince Wei of Chu, was made general of the guards, heading the colonel of the northern armies; Prince Huang of Xiapi was made director of the secretariat; Duke Yao of Dong’an was made left vice director of the secretariat and advanced in enfeoffment to prince of Dong’an.

value.zh: 督將侯者千八十一人。
value.en: One thousand eighty-one officers of commander rank or above were ennobled as marquises.
value.literal: Supervisors and generals who were marquises numbered one thousand eighty-one persons.

value.zh: 庚戌，免東安王繇及東平王楙，繇徙帶方。
value.en: Princes Yao and Mao were stripped of their posts, and Yao was banished to Daifang on the Korean frontier.
value.literal: On the gengxu day, Prince Yao of Dong’an and Prince Mao of Dongping were dismissed from office; Yao was transferred to Daifang.

value.zh: 六月，賈后矯詔使楚王瑋殺太宰、汝南王亮，太保、菑陽公衛瓘。
value.en: In the sixth month Empress Jia forged orders that sent Prince Wei of Chu to murder Prince Liang of Runan, the grand steward, and Duke Wei Guan of Ziyang, the grand guardian.
value.literal: In the sixth month, Empress Jia forged an edict causing Prince Wei of Chu to kill Grand Steward, Prince Liang of Runan, and Grand Guardian, Duke Wei Guan of Ziyang.

value.zh: 乙丑，以瑋擅害亮、瓘，殺之。
value.en: On the yichou day Prince Wei was executed for having murdered Liang and Guan without authorization.
value.literal: On the yichou day, because Wei had on his own authority harmed Liang and Guan, he was killed.

value.zh: 曲赦洛陽。
value.en: Luoyang received a limited amnesty.
value.literal: A partial amnesty was proclaimed for Luoyang.

value.zh: 以廣陵王師劉寔爲太子太保，司空、隴西王泰錄尚書事。
value.en: Liu Shi became grand guardian to the crown prince, and Prince Tai of Longxi, still minister of works, took charge of secretariat business.
value.literal: Preceptor to the Prince of Guangling, Liu Shi, was made grand guardian of the heir apparent; Minister of Works, Prince Tai of Longxi, recorded the affairs of the secretariat.

value.zh: 月五星犯列舍經星變附見
value.en: The Moon and the Five Planets Transgressing the Lodges and Classical Stars, with Supplementary Notes on Celestial Portents.
value.literal: Transgressions of the Moon and the Five Planets against the Lodges and Classical Stars; appended observations on anomalies.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月，客星在紫宮。
value.en: Taixi 1 April guest star in Purple Palace.
value.literal: In Taixi 1 fourth month a guest star stood in Purple Forbidden.

value.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "It means war and mourning."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be armies and mourning.

value.zh: 太康未，武帝耽宴遊，多疾病。
value.en: Late Taikang Wu feasted into illness.
value.literal: Near Taikang’s end Emperor Wu indulged feasting and fell chronically ill.

value.zh: 是月己酉，帝崩。
value.en: Jiyou that month ended Emperor Wu.
value.literal: That month on jiyou the emperor died.

value.zh: 永平元年，賈后誅楊駿及其黨與，皆夷三族，楊太后亦見弑。
value.en: Yongping purge slew Yang clan.
value.literal: In Yongping 1 Empress Jia executed Yang Jun and faction to third kin—even Empress Dowager Yang was murdered.

value.zh: 又誅汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋，王室兵喪之應也。
value.en: Further kin slaughter followed.
value.literal: She also killed Prince Runan Liang, Grand Guardian Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—responses of martial mourning for the royal house.

value.zh: 《書》曰：「唐虞稽古，建官惟百。」
value.en: The Book of Documents says: "When Tang and Yu looked back to antiquity, they created no more than a hundred offices."
value.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Tang and Yu examined antiquity; they established offices numbering only one hundred."

value.zh: 所以獎導民萌，裁成庶政。
value.en: That was how they encouraged the people and gave shape to the affairs of state.
value.literal: By this means they encouraged and guided the common people, and brought order to every branch of government.

value.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，聖人則之。」
value.en: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven displays signs; the sage patterns himself on them."
value.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven hangs forth images; the sage takes them as his model."

value.zh: 執法在南宮之右，上相處端門之外，而鳥龍居位，雲火垂名，前史詳之，其以尚矣。
value.en: Justice lay to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister waited beyond the Duan Gate; bird and dragon offices held rank with cloud and fire as their emblems—prior histories lay it out clearly, and the grandeur speaks for itself.
value.literal: Law sat to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister took station beyond the Duan Gate; the Bird and Dragon offices held their posts, cloud and fire lending their names—earlier histories spell this out in detail, and the dignity of it is plain.

value.zh: 黃帝置三公之秩，以親黎元，少昊配九扈之名，以為農正，命重黎於天地，詔融冥於水火，則可得而言焉。
value.en: The Yellow Emperor created the Three Dukes to draw near to the people; Shaohao aligned the Nine Hu titles with agricultural oversight; Chong and Li received Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming received fire and water—and such patterns can be put into words.
value.literal: The Yellow Emperor instituted the ranks of the Three Dukes to stay close to the black-haired masses; Shaohao paired the Nine Hu bird-names with the office of director of agriculture; Chong and Li were charged with Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming were charged with fire and water—these arrangements can indeed be described.

value.zh: 伊尹曰：「三公調陰陽，九卿通寒暑，大夫知人事，列士去其私。」
value.en: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers track the seasons; grand officers attend to human affairs; ranked officers put private interest aside."
value.literal: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers watch cold and heat; grand officers understand human affairs; ranked officers rid themselves of selfishness."

value.zh: 而成湯居亳，初置二相，以伊尹、仲虺為之，凡厥樞會，仰承君命。
value.en: When Tang of Shang made Bo his seat, he first set up two chancellors—Yi Yin and Zhong Hui—and on every pivot they carried out the sovereign's will.
value.literal: When Cheng Tang ruled from Bo, he first created two chancellors and appointed Yi Yin and Zhong Hui to them; on every critical matter they looked upward to receive the ruler's commands.

value.zh: 總及周武下車，成康垂則，六卿分職，二公弘化，咸樹司存，各題標準，苟非其道，人弗虛榮。
value.en: Under King Wu and the models left by Cheng and Kang, the Six Ministers split the labor, the Two Dukes carried royal influence abroad, every bureau had its charter, and no one claimed idle honors without the right conduct.
value.literal: Altogether, when King Wu of Zhou stepped down from his chariot to rule, Cheng and Kang handed down norms; the Six Ministers divided duties; the Two Dukes spread transformation; each office kept its place and measure; if it were not the proper Way, people did not vainly seek glory.

value.zh: 貽厥孫謀，其固本也如此。
value.en: They anchored the dynasty by planning for generations yet unborn.
value.literal: They left plans for their descendants; thus they secured the foundation.

value.zh: 及秦變周官，漢遵嬴舊，或隨時適用，或因務遷革，霸王之典，義在於斯，既獲厥安，所謂得其時制者也。
value.en: Qin refashioned Zhou's bureaucracy; Han largely kept Qin's frame while tweaking it for the moment—the logic of strong rule was there—and stability meant institutions matched their age.
value.literal: When Qin altered the Zhou offices and Han followed the Ying-clan precedent, sometimes adapting to the times, sometimes shifting with practical needs—the norms of hegemons and kings lay herein; once stability was gained, this is what is called obtaining timely institutions.

value.zh: 四征興於漢代，四安起于魏初，四鎮通於柔遠，四平止於喪亂，其渡遼、淩江，輕車、強弩，式揚遐外，用表攻伐，興而復毀，厥號彌繁。
value.en: Han invented the Four Expeditions; Wei at its outset the Four Pacifications; Four Garrisons stretched toward distant peoples; Four Peace posts vanished when chaos returned. Epithets like Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow brandished force beyond the borders for campaigns—created, scrapped, then multiplied until the catalogue grew tangled.
value.literal: The Four Expeditions arose in Han; the Four Pacifications began at the start of Wei; the Four Garrisons reached outward to soothe the distant; the Four Peace offices ended with turmoil and disorder; as for Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow—they displayed might afar and signaled campaigns—raised up and then abolished, their titles grew ever more numerous.

value.zh: 及當塗得志，克平諸夏，初有軍師祭酒，參掌戎律。
value.en: Once the Cao regime triumphed and pacified the heartland, it introduced the army adviser libationer to share oversight of military law.
value.literal: When the house at Dangtu achieved its ambition and subdued the Central Plain, there first appeared the army adviser libationer, who jointly handled military regulations.

value.zh: 建安十三年，罷漢台司，更置丞相，而以曹公居之，用兼端揆。
value.en: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an (208), the Han ministerial posts were abolished, the chancellorship was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.
value.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, the Han terrace ministers were abolished; the chancellor was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.

value.zh: 孫吳、劉蜀，多依漢制，雖復臨時命氏，而無忝舊章。
value.en: Wu and Shu largely kept Han models; occasional improvised titles notwithstanding, they stayed within the classical mold.
value.literal: Eastern Wu and Liu Bei's Shu largely followed Han institutions; though they sometimes improvised titles on the spot, they did not shame the old statutes.

value.zh: 世祖武皇帝即位之初，以安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅，王祥為太保，司馬望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，世所謂八公同辰，攀雲附翼者也。
value.en: At his accession, Emperor Wu named Sima Fu Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang Grand Guardian, Sima Wang Minister of War, He Zeng Minister of Education, Xun Yi Minister of Works, Shi Bao Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian Grand General—the storied eight dukes of a single hour, men who rose by riding imperial favor.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu the Shizu first ascended the throne, he appointed Prince Fu of Anping as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang as Grand Guardian, Sima Wang as Minister of War, He Zeng as Minister of Education, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian as Grand General—what the age called the eight dukes sharing one hour, climbing clouds and attaching wings.

value.zh: 若乃成乎棟宇，非一枝之勢；
value.en: Raising the whole hall takes more than one timber;
value.literal: As for completing roof-beams and rafters—it is not the strength of a single branch;

value.zh: 處乎經綸，稱萬夫之敵。
value.en: true stewardship of the realm earns the title match for ten thousand.
value.literal: to dwell in ordering the realm is to be called a match for ten thousand men.

value.zh: 或牽羊以葉於夢，或垂釣以申其道，或空桑以獻其術，或操版以啟其心。
value.en: Some arrived through dreams of sheep and grain; some through fishing metaphors; some from humble soil with a craft to sell; some by presenting the royal tablet and winning trust.
value.literal: Some led sheep and answered a leaf in a dream; some angled with a hook to proclaim their Way; some offered their arts from an empty mulberry; some grasped the tablet to open the ruler's mind.

value.zh: 臥龍飛鴻，方金擬璧，秦奚、鄭產，楚材晉用，斯亦曩時之良具，其又昭彰者焉。
value.en: Hidden dragons and soaring swans, talents weighed like gold against jade—Qin Xi, Zheng Chan, and Chu talent employed by Jin: these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.
value.literal: The sleeping dragon, the soaring wild goose—square metal compared to round jade; the shepherd of Qin, the prodigy of Zheng; Chu talent employed by Jin—these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.

value.zh: 宣王既誅曹爽，政由己出，網羅英俊，以備天官。
value.en: After Sima Yi eliminated Cao Shuang, he ruled in his own name and stocked every court post with talent.
value.literal: Once Prince Xuan had executed Cao Shuang, government proceeded from himself alone; he gathered capable men to fill the celestial offices.

value.zh: 及蘭卿受羈，貴公顯戮，雖復策名魏氏，而乃心皇晉。
value.en: When fine officers were seized and great nobles died in public execution, names might still stand with Wei but hearts had already turned to Jin.
value.literal: When worthy ministers were placed under restraint and eminent dukes suffered public execution—though they still bore registration under the Wei, their hearts were with the august Jin.

value.zh: 及文王纂業，初啟晉台，始置二衛，有前驅養由之弩；
value.en: When Sima Zhao extended the family work and founded the Jin apparatus, he created the Two Guards with vanguard crossbows worthy of Yang Youji.
value.literal: When King Wen continued the enterprise and first opened the Jin terrace, he began setting up the Two Guards, including front-vanguard crossbows like Yang Youji's.

value.zh: 及設三部，有熊渠佽飛之眾。
value.en: When the Three Corps were established, there were masses like those of Xiong Qu and Ci Fei.
value.literal: When the Three Departments were established, there were masses like the royal swimmers of Xiong Qu.

value.zh: 是以武帝龍飛，乘茲奮翼，猶武王以周之十亂而理殷民者也。
value.en: Thus Emperor Wu's rise—vaulting on these preparations—matched King Wu deploying his ten able assistants to rule the former Shang subjects.
value.literal: Therefore when Emperor Wu ascended like a dragon, riding this to beat his wings, it was like King Wu of Zhou using the Zhou's ten ministers to govern the Yin people.

value.zh: 是以泰始盡于太康，喬柯茂葉，來居斯位；
value.en: From the Taishi era through Taikang, imposing figures filled those ranks;
value.literal: Thus from Taishi through Taikang, tall trees with lush foliage came to occupy these posts;

value.zh: 自太興訖於建元，南金北銑，用處茲秩。
value.en: from Daxing to Jianyuan, the finest metal south and north filled those offices.
value.literal: from Daxing down to Jianyuan, southern gold and northern ore were employed in these ranks.

value.zh: 雖未擬乎夔拊龍言，天工人代，亦庶幾乎任官惟賢，蒞事惟能者也。
value.en: They fell short of the sage-kings' marriage of Heaven's work to human agency, yet they neared the ideal: office by virtue, tasks by competence.
value.literal: Though they did not equal Kui's drumming and Long's pronouncements—Heaven's work and man's substitute—they approximated appoint officials only for worth, approach affairs only by ability.

value.zh: 太子太傅、少傅，皆古官也。
value.en: Heir tutors were classical posts.
value.literal: Grand tutor and junior tutor of the heir apparent—both were ancient offices.

value.zh: 泰始三年，武帝始建官，各置一人，尚未置詹事，官事無大小，皆由二傅，並有功曹、主簿、五官。
value.en: In the third year of Taishi (267), Emperor Wu first created these offices, one post each; before any household supervisor was appointed, all business, large or small, passed through the two tutors, who also had merit clerks, chief clerks, and gatekeeper officers.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi Emperor Wu first established the offices, each one post; not yet appointing a household supervisor—office business large or small all passed through the two tutors, who also had merit clerks, chief clerks, and gatekeeper officers.

value.zh: 太傅中二千石，少傅二千石。
value.en: Senior tutor drew near two thousand shi; junior tutor two thousand.
value.literal: Grand tutor at salary comparable to two thousand shi; junior tutor at two thousand shi.

value.zh: 其訓導者，太傅在前，少傅在後。
value.en: Instruction lined up senior tutor forward, junior aft.
value.literal: Those who instructed—grand tutor in front, junior tutor behind.

value.zh: 皇太子先拜，諸傅然後答之。
value.en: The crown prince bowed first; tutors returned the courtesy.
value.literal: The imperial heir first bowed; the tutors then answered.

value.zh: 武帝后以儲副體尊，遂命諸公居之；
value.en: Once the heir's rank swelled, grandees filled those chairs;
value.literal: Later Emperor Wu because the heir's station was august ordered various dukes to occupy the posts;

value.zh: 以本位重，故或行或領。
value.en: weight meant some served full-time, some doubled other posts.
value.literal: because the posts were weighty, therefore some served in person and some held concurrent titles.

value.zh: 時侍中任愷，武帝所親敬，復使領之，蓋一時之制也。
value.en: Ren Kai briefly doubled duty—a court expedient.
value.literal: At the time attendant Ren Kai, whom Emperor Wu personally favored and respected, was also made to oversee them—probably an arrangement of the moment.

value.zh: 咸甯元年，以給事黃門侍郎楊珧為詹事，掌宮事，二傅不復領官屬。
value.en: 275 CE Yang Yao became household supervisor so tutors shed staff.
value.literal: In the first year of Xianning gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates Yang Yao was made household supervisor handling palace business; the two tutors no longer supervised subordinates.

value.zh: 及楊珧為衛將軍，領少傅，省詹事，遂崇廣傅訓，命太尉賈充領太保，司空齊王攸領太傅，所置吏屬復如舊。
value.en: When Yang Yao became General of the Guards and concurrently Junior Tutor, the household supervisor was abolished and tutor instruction was expanded: Grand Commandant Jia Chong was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Guardian, and Minister of Works Prince You of Qi as Grand Tutor; the appointed clerical staff returned to the old pattern.
value.literal: When Yang Yao became General of the Guards and concurrently Junior Tutor, the household supervisor was abolished; tutor instruction was then enlarged—Grand Commandant Jia Chong was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Guardian, and Minister of Works Prince You of Qi as Grand Tutor; the appointed clerical staff returned as before.

value.zh: 二傅進賢兩梁冠，黑介幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，食奉日三斛。
value.en: Tutors wore two-ridged caps, black kerchiefs, seasonal robes, jade, three hu daily.
value.literal: The two tutors wore two-beam advanced-worth caps, black scarves, five-seasons court dress, dark aquamarine jade, daily grain allowance three hu.

value.zh: 太康二年，始給春賜絹五十匹，秋絹百匹，綿百斤。
value.en: 281 CE added seasonal silk and cotton allotments.
value.literal: In the second year of Taikang they began granting spring silk fifty bolts, autumn silk one hundred bolts, cotton one hundred jin.

value.zh: 其後太尉汝南王亮、車騎將軍楊駿、司空衛瓘、石鑒皆領傅保，猶不置詹事，以終武帝之世。
value.en: Afterward, the Grand Commandant Prince Liang of Runan, General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jun, Minister of Works Wei Guan, and Shi Jian all concurrently held tutor-guardian posts, but no household supervisor was appointed through the end of Emperor Wu's reign.
value.literal: Afterward Grand Commandant Prince Liang of Runan, General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jun, Minister of Works Wei Guan, and Shi Jian all held tutor-guardian posts; still no household supervisor was appointed through Emperor Wu's reign.

value.zh: 惠帝元康元年，復置詹事，二傅給菜田六頃，田騶六人，立夏後不及田者，食奉一年。
value.en: 291 CE revived the supervisor and granted tutors vegetable plots like ministers.
value.literal: Emperor Hui in the first year of Yuankang restored household supervisor; the two tutors received six qing vegetable land and six field runners; if after beginning of summer land had not been awarded, one year's salary instead.

value.zh: 置丞一人，秩千石；
value.en: One deputy at one thousand shi;
value.literal: One assistant was placed at rank one thousand shi;

value.zh: 主簿、五官掾、功曹史、主記門下史、錄事、戶曹法曹倉曹賊曹功曹書佐、門下亭長、門下書佐、省事各一人，給赤耳安車一乘。
value.en: full tutor household staff plus a red-eared carriage.
value.literal: chief clerk, gatekeeper officers, merit clerk, chief recorder, gate clerks, recorder, household office, law office, granary office, thieves office, merit clerk assistants, gate precinct chief, gate document clerks, miscellaneous clerks—one each; one red-eared secure carriage granted.

value.zh: 及湣懷建官，乃置六傅，三太、三少，以景帝諱師，故改太師為太保，通省尚書事，詹事文書關由六傅。
value.en: Minhuai's six tutors—taboo turned instructor into guardian—shared Secretariat oversight.
value.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai established offices, six tutors were set—three senior and three junior—because of the taboo on Emperor Jing's name Shi, therefore Grand Instructor was changed to senior guardian, jointly overseeing Secretariat business; household paperwork passed through all six tutors.

value.zh: 然自元康之後，諸傅或二或三，或四或六，及永康中復不置詹事也。
value.en: Tutor counts fluctuated; Yongkang dropped the supervisor again.
value.literal: Yet from Yuankang onward tutors numbered two, three, four, or six; by Yongkang household supervisor was again absent.

value.zh: 自太安已來置詹事，終孝懷之世。
value.en: Tai'an forward kept supervisors through the prince's fall.
value.literal: From Tai'an onward household supervisor was set through Emperor Xiaohuai's reign.

value.zh: 渡江之後，有太傅少傅，不立師保。
value.en: South of the river kept grand and junior tutors only.
value.literal: After crossing the Yangzi there were grand and junior tutors but no instructor or guardian titles.

value.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂
value.en: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.
value.literal: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.

value.zh: 惠帝元康二年二月，巴西郡界草皆生華，結子如麥，可食。
value.en: In the second month of Yuankang 2 under Emperor Hui, Baxi grasses flowered and set edible wheat-like seed.
value.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 2, second month — grasses throughout Baxi commandery all flowered and bore seeds like wheat, which could be eaten.

value.zh: 時帝初即位，楚王瑋矯詔誅汝南王亮及太保衛瓘，帝不能察。
value.en: Sima Wei's coup caught the new throne blind.
value.literal: The emperor had just mounted the throne; Prince Chu Wei forged edicts killing Prince Runan Liang and grand tutor Wei Guan — the emperor could not investigate.

value.zh: 今非時草結實，此恆燠寬舒之罰。
value.en: Untimely grain on weeds bespoke thermal slackness.
value.literal: Now grass fruits out of season — punishment of constant heat and lax ease.

value.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
value.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
value.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

value.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
value.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
value.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

value.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
value.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
value.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

value.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
value.en: Later ages styled her queen.
value.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

value.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
value.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
value.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

value.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
value.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
value.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

value.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
value.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
value.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

value.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
value.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
value.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

value.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

value.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
value.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
value.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

value.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
value.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
value.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

value.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
value.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
value.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

value.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
value.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
value.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

value.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
value.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
value.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

value.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
value.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
value.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

value.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
value.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
value.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

value.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
value.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
value.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

value.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
value.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
value.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

value.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
value.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
value.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

value.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
value.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
value.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

value.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
value.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
value.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

value.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
value.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
value.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

value.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
value.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
value.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

value.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
value.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
value.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

value.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
value.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
value.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

value.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
value.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
value.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

value.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
value.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
value.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

value.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
value.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
value.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

value.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
value.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
value.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

value.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
value.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
value.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

value.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
value.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
value.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

value.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
value.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.
value.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.

value.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
value.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

value.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
value.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
value.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

value.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
value.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
value.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

value.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
value.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
value.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

value.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
value.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
value.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

value.zh: 帝以皇太子不堪奉大統，密以語后。
value.en: Believing the crown prince unfit to inherit the realm, he confided as much privately to the empress.
value.literal: The emperor considered the crown prince unable to uphold the great line and secretly spoke of it to the empress.

value.zh: 后曰：「立嫡以長不以賢，豈可動乎？」
value.en: She replied, “The eldest legitimate son succeeds regardless of talent—how can we undo that?”
value.literal: The empress said: “Establishing the heir depends on seniority among legitimate sons, not on talent—how can that be altered?”

value.zh: 初，賈充妻郭氏使賂后，求以女為太子妃。
value.en: Earlier Jia Chong’s wife Lady Guo had bribed her to secure her daughter as crown princess.
value.literal: At first Jia Chong’s wife Lady Guo sent bribes to the empress, seeking to make her daughter crown princess.

value.zh: 及議太子婚，帝欲娶衛瓘女。
value.en: When the heir’s marriage came under debate, the emperor favored Wei Guan’s daughter.
value.literal: When discussing the crown prince’s marriage, the emperor wished to take Wei Guan’s daughter.

value.zh: 然后盛稱賈后有淑德，又密使太子太傅荀顗進言，上乃聽之。
value.en: The empress loudly praised Lady Jia’s virtue and secretly had Grand Tutor Xun Yi speak for her, so the emperor yielded.
value.literal: But the empress greatly praised Consort Jia’s virtuous conduct, and also secretly had Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince Xun Yi speak; the sovereign then consented.

value.zh: 泰始中，帝博選良家以充後宮，先下書禁天下嫁娶，使宦者乘使車，給騶騎，馳傳州郡，召充選者使后揀擇。
value.en: Midway through Taishi he cast a wide net for palace women, banned commoners from marrying, sent eunuchs in official carriages with escorts racing along post roads to every commandery, and had the candidates presented to the empress for her verdict.
value.literal: In the Taishi era the emperor broadly selected good families to fill the rear palace; first he issued a document forbidding marriage in the realm, had eunuchs ride dispatch coaches provided with outriders, gallop relay orders to provinces and commanderies, summon those filling selection and had the empress pick and choose.

value.zh: 后性妒，惟取潔白長大，其端正美麗者並不見留。
value.en: Jealous by nature, she kept only plain, towering girls and rejected every truly lovely face.
value.literal: The empress was by nature jealous; she only took those fair and tall; those properly beautiful were none of them retained.

value.zh: 時卞藩女有美色，帝掩扇謂后曰：「卞氏女佳。」
value.en: When Bian Fan’s daughter proved breathtaking, the emperor hid behind his fan and said, “The Bian girl is a jewel.”
value.literal: At the time Bian Fan’s daughter had beautiful looks; the emperor hid behind a fan and said to the empress: “Bian’s daughter is excellent.”

value.zh: 后曰：「藩三世后族，其女不可枉以卑位。」
value.en: The empress answered, “Three generations of Bians have supplied empresses—such a bride cannot be parked in a petty title.”
value.literal: The empress said: “The Bian clan for three generations has been empress kin—their daughter cannot be slighted with low rank.”

value.zh: 帝乃止。
value.en: He dropped the matter.
value.literal: The emperor then stopped.

value.zh: 司徒李胤、鎮軍大將軍胡奮、廷尉諸葛沖、太僕臧權、侍中馮蓀、秘書郎左思及世族子女並充三夫人九嬪之列。
value.en: The daughters of Li Yin, Hu Fen, Zhuge Chong, Zang Quan, Feng Sun, Zuo Si, and other great houses were placed among the Three Ladies and the Nine Concubines.
value.literal: Minister of Education Li Yin, General Who Guards the Army Hu Fen, Commandant of Justice Zhuge Chong, Grand Coachman Zang Quan, Palace Attendant Feng Sun, Secretary Court Gentleman Zuo Si, and daughters of eminent clans together filled the ranks of three ladies and nine bin.

value.zh: 司、冀、兗、豫四州二千石將吏家，補良人以下。
value.en: From Si, Ji, Yan, and Yu the daughters of prefects and local officers filled the ranks below Good Woman.
value.literal: Families of two-thousand-shi commandery officials in Si, Ji, Yan, and Yu four prefectures supplied ranks below liangren.

value.zh: 名家盛族子女，多敗衣瘁貌以避之。
value.en: Great families dressed their girls in rags and smeared their faces to dodge the draft.
value.literal: Sons and daughters of famous houses and great clans mostly wore tattered clothes and haggard looks to avoid it.

value.zh: 惠賈皇后諱南風，平陽人也，小名時。
value.en: Empress Jia Nanfeng of Pingyang—pet name Shi.
value.literal: Empress Jia of Hui, taboo Nanfeng, native of Pingyang, childhood name Shi.
